statement: Explicit evidence-level honesty statement: the E4 repair verification is Level 4 only (against the reference implementation), NOT Level 5, because the real running EKP has no inquiry register at all and Ask(p) cannot be observed there -- claiming Level 5 would repeat the exact error (validating a specification only against itself) that Step 280 was commissioned to eliminate.

anchor: ΔR(B) is the smallest extension satisfying M1 ∧ M2 ∧ M3.
statement: Final minimality conclusion restated in prose: ΔR(B), the inquiry register Q_t, is the smallest extension of the three candidates that jointly satisfies necessity (M1), irreducibility (M2), and no-redundant-distinction (M3).

Step 280 is executed via a seven-phase plan: (1) faithfully implement Step 279 components 1-15, (2) implement the K/Sigma/T layer under test, (3) build >=36 stratified test cases with >=20% negative, (4) execute E1-E24, (5) execute F1-F13(+F4b), (6) probe the real EKP and compute statistics against 10 critical conditions, (7) populate the closure matrix with observed evidence only.

anchor: no fallbacks · no silent repair · no implicit boolean conversion (the rule evaluator raises on any verdict outside {PASS,DENY,CONDITIONAL,UNKNOWN,CONFLICT}) · failures reported as failures · Level 4 ≠ Level 5 maintained throughout.
statement: Step 280's discipline: no fallbacks, no silent repair, no implicit boolean conversion (the rule evaluator raises on any verdict outside the closed set {PASS,DENY,CONDITIONAL,UNKNOWN,CONFLICT}), failures are reported as failures, and the Level-4-vs-Level-5 evidence distinction is maintained throughout.

anchor: E4 | Missingness | FAIL | 4 | not-asked = INDISTINGUISHABLE from absent; orphan has no K representation
statement: E4 (Missingness) FAILS at evidence Level 4: 'not-asked' is indistinguishable from 'absent' in the executed model, and the orphan construct has no representation in K at all.

experiment.hypothesis: the K representation can distinguish not-asked from asked-but-absent, and can represent orphan assertions
experiment.setup: executed reference implementation of K/Sigma/T under Step 279's design
experiment.assumptions: K = (assertion set, relation set) as specified by Step 279
experiment.inputs: constructed cases exercising not-asked, asked-absent, and orphan conditions
experiment.method: direct execution and comparison of resulting representations
experiment.result: not-asked and asked-absent both map to the same observable value; orphan has no K representation
experiment.limitations: executed against reference implementation, not against the real EKP for this specific test

anchor: E20 | Statistics | BLOCKED | 0 | no (Ω,ℱ,P) anywhere; str is ORDINAL
statement: E20 (Statistics) is BLOCKED at Level 0: no probability space (Omega,F,P) exists anywhere in the theory, and the strength construct is merely ORDINAL, so calibration is inexecutable.

anchor: 22 PASS · 1 FAIL · 1 BLOCKED. Level ≥4: 21/24. Level 5: 8/24.
statement: Aggregate E-suite result: 22 PASS, 1 FAIL, 1 BLOCKED across E1-E24; 21/24 reach evidence Level >=4 and only 8/24 reach Level 5 (real-environment observation).

anchor: E17 | Governance | PASS | 3 | τ=5 — SIMULATED, no real multi-node system
statement: E17 (Governance, multi-node convergence time tau=5) passes only at Level 3, explicitly flagged as SIMULATED because no real multi-node system exists to observe.

anchor: FP = 0. Across every negative control — no authority, revoked authority, expired policy, missing policy, policy conflict, authority conflict, unauthorized mutation — not one was wrongly Permitted.
statement: The load-bearing falsification statistic: across every constructed negative control (no authority, revoked authority, expired policy, missing policy, policy conflict, authority conflict, unauthorized mutation), the false-positive rate is 0 -- none was wrongly Permitted.

experiment.hypothesis: the policy/authority evaluator never permits an action under a negative-control condition
experiment.setup: 13 falsification cases F1-F13(+F4b) covering authority/policy negative controls
experiment.assumptions: policy and authority objects as formalized by Step 279
experiment.method: execute the evaluator and compare observed verdict to expected verdict
experiment.interpretation: strong evidence the evaluator's denial logic is sound under tested conditions
experiment.limitations: F12 is simulated (no real multi-node deployment); F8 could not be attempted by mutation because the policy object is frozen at the type level

anchor: F8 could not even be attempted by mutation — the policy object is frozen, so unauthorized mutation fails at the type level rather than the governance level. Recorded as a stronger-than-required result, and as a caveat: a frozen dataclass is not evidence that a real system would refuse.
statement: F8's PASS is caveated: the policy object being a frozen dataclass means unauthorized mutation fails at the type level, not the governance level -- a stronger-than-required result that is explicitly NOT evidence a real system would refuse the same mutation.

anchor: F9 was tested against STORED state, not the returned status, as the specification demands.
statement: F9 (duplicate version rejection) is deliberately tested against the STORED state rather than the returned status, per the specification's requirement, and stored count remains 1->1 after a rejected duplicate.

anchor: Replay is the strongest computational result in Step 280 and has no real-environment counterpart.
statement: All seven replay properties (deterministic replay, fold-equivalence, historical policy selection, replay-uses-historical-not-current-policy, policy-version preservation, authority-history preservation, provenance-survives-replay-at-t=0) PASS computationally, but real-system replay is NOT OBSERVABLE at Level 1 -- git holds history but the platform itself does not model replay -- so this is assessed as the strongest computational result with no real-environment counterpart.

experiment.hypothesis: Replay(H) is deterministic and equals fold(T,empty,H), and replay correctly uses historical rather than current policy/authority
experiment.setup: constructed history H with policy version changes and an authority revocation
experiment.assumptions: T (transition function) and H (history) as defined by Step 279
experiment.inputs: a history sequence including policy activation events at different times
experiment.method: execute Replay(H) twice and compare; compute PolicyAt at two different historical times
experiment.result: Replay(H)==Replay(H); PolicyAt(2026-03)=v1, PolicyAt(2026-08)=v2; old verdict computed under v1
experiment.interpretation: replay is deterministic and historically faithful in the reference implementation
experiment.limitations: no real multi-node/production system exists against which to observe replay (Level 1 only)

anchor: reproducibility here means *the same harness gives the same answer*. It does **not** establish that an independent implementer would obtain the same result — that is Level 6, and **no Level-6 evidence exists.**
statement: Reproducibility as measured (same harness, byte-identical re-runs, no wall-clock/RNG, stable content-addressed ids) is explicitly distinguished from Level-6 reproducibility (an independent implementer obtaining the same result), for which no evidence exists.

anchor: E4 missingness | T — theory defect | the model, not the code, lacks the distinction
statement: Error taxonomy classification: E4's missingness failure is a T (theory defect) because the model itself, not the implementing code, lacks the not-asked/absent distinction; E20's calibration failure is likewise T (no probability space defined anywhere); the 15 NOT OBSERVABLE constructs are I (implementation limitation, the EKP was built for governed documents not evidence-bearing claims); E17/F12 simulation is E (empirical anomaly, no multi-node deployment exists to observe).

anchor: No mismatch was discarded as an implementation detail without classification.
statement: Discipline statement: no observed mismatch between expected and observed test results is discarded as a mere implementation detail without an explicit T/I/E classification.
